reasoning:
The report itself seems to resist a clean rule—across rounds, sometimes earliest-first explains the data, sometimes latest-first does, and the one factor that does separate them is whether distractor cubes of other colors are present. I wonder if "first" doesn't refer to counting order at all but to something else entirely, like which target got a cube placed on it first.

Without more episodes to test against, I can't validate any hypothesis, and committing nothing seems like the honest answer here. I'll note the distractor-cube pattern and the oddity of a recorded drop onto a target never actually used in the demo as leads for future rounds, but leave the edit uncommitted since I can't verify any ordinal rule confidently.

revision.refused: Nothing is committed this round. The report asks for nothing beyond what it already refused: the two failed drop steps fit a backward count of the demonstration placements, and the three passing steps fit the forward count the rule now prescribes. That is the same split seen in round 1 (two forward, two backward, one onto a target never placed on) and round 2 (three forward, two otherwise). Reversing the count, or adding a clause keyed on the presence of distractor cubes, would trade the passing steps for the failing ones and undo the explicit forward-counting procedure committed in round 2, so neither is adopted. The forward count remains the stated rule because it is the plain reading of the goal and fits the most recorded drops in every round so far. One note for the annotator in later rounds rather than an edit now: the recurring mismatch, including the round-1 drop onto a target the demonstration never used, suggests the ordinal may index something other than placement order (for example a property of the targets themselves or of the whole demonstration rather than of the goal-named cube's releases). If a later minibatch shows one feature of the demonstration frames that separates the two conventions, that is the rule to write; a feature the report itself does not believe is a cause is not written in.
